adoption.body: Current AI use is reported by 24.6% of businesses, compared with 28.6% expecting use within six months, a 4.0-percentage-point gap between deployment and intent. Reported use is much higher among adults: 60.8% of those ages 18–64 use some generative AI, although that consumer measure is not directly comparable with organization-level use of AI more generally. A newly reported enterprise study found adoption outpacing AI assurance, identifying assurance as a separate implementation issue rather than simply another measure of adoption.
adoption.headline: Business AI use remains below near-term intentions as assurance emerges as a separate concern

macro.body: Hardware growth is becoming less concentrated in the semiconductor segment. Computer and peripheral-equipment output accelerated materially to 12.0%, with capacity utilization rising to 84.5%. Semiconductor and electronic-component output still grew faster, at 15.3%, but its growth and utilization both fell materially, leaving utilization at 74.4%. Reuters reported, citing sources, that TSMC tightened China AI-chip curbs as new U.S. rules closed a manufacturing loophole. The development concerns access to specific advanced chips, which can tighten even as broad semiconductor utilization eases. The infrastructure pipeline is large, but projects and planned generation are not yet delivered capacity. Available records place 1,556 data-center sites in development, equal to 0.51 times the operating count. Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, compared with 1.8% for total retail demand, and net planned generation additions through the pipeline horizon total 227.6 GW. Utility Dive reported that PJM was urged to delay a base-capacity auction until data centers were cut from its forecast. The request shows that large-load assumptions are consequential and disputed in grid planning; it does not establish that PJM’s forecast is wrong. The market signal and economy-wide payoff remain less clear. The AI Equity Index fell materially to 31.2 even though 64.2% of covered companies have positive one-year returns, combining broad participation with a weaker aggregate signal. Productivity grew 2.1% and real output 2.3%, while real hourly compensation rose 0.6%. Reuters reported that the Federal Reserve’s Jefferson said AI was boosting inflation and that its productivity effect may come in the future. The current figures show positive aggregate performance, but not a distinct AI contribution.
macro.headline: Hardware growth broadens, but infrastructure delivery and the economic payoff remain uncertain

market.body: Positive one-year returns now extend to 64.2% of covered companies, a slight increase. Yet the median return eased to 10.4%, the AI Equity Index fell materially to 31.2, and average sector trading pressure edged up to 41.0. CNBC reported that Palo Alto Networks shares surged after an earnings beat, higher guidance and a $4.5 billion AI deal. Strong company-specific news can still draw a sharp response, but the broader readings combine wide participation with a weaker index and lower typical return.
market.headline: Market breadth holds up as the aggregate AI signal weakens

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: The AI Equity Index rose slightly to 32.5, while average sector trading pressure eased to 40.7. Beneath those top-line readings, the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns fell materially to 60.8%, and the median return declined to 8.7%. The aggregate signal improved modestly, but participation in gains and typical performance both weakened.

headline.text: The aggregate AI market signal edges higher even as gains become less broad

body.text: Current AI use is reported by 24.6% of businesses, while 28.6% expect to use it within six months. The four-percentage-point gap shows that stated near-term plans still exceed deployment. Among adults ages 18–64, 60.8% report some generative-AI use, although that consumer measure covers a different population and technology category. EE Times reported that Palo Alto Networks expanded into enterprise AI through a $4.5 billion deal. The transaction shows a supplier adding enterprise exposure; it does not establish that business adoption has accelerated.

headline.text: Business AI use remains below near-term intent as Palo Alto expands into enterprise AI
The physical pipeline remains large, while business use and market gains are less broad

paragraphs.text: The physical buildout remains substantial. Output grew 15.3% for semiconductors and electronic components and 12.0% for computers and peripherals. Available project records show 1,556 data-center sites in development, equal to about half the operating count. The electricity system illustrates why a large pipeline is not the same as delivered capacity: 2,061 GW is in active interconnection queues, but only 24.2% has reached executed-agreement or construction stages, and just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation.

Deployment is less extensive among businesses. Current AI use stands at 24.6%, compared with 28.6% expecting use within six months. Adults ages 18–64 report some generative-AI use at a much higher rate of 60.8%, although the consumer and business measures are not directly comparable. EE Times reported that Palo Alto Networks expanded into enterprise AI through a $4.5 billion deal. That move reflects supplier competition for enterprise demand, not proof that adoption is accelerating.

The market now presents a mixed signal. The AI Equity Index edged up to 32.5 and sector trading pressure eased, but the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns fell materially to 60.8%, while the median return declined to 8.7%. Economy-wide productivity and real output grew 2.1% and 2.3%, respectively, while real hourly compensation rose 0.6%. These measures remain positive in aggregate, but they do not isolate a distinct AI contribution.

You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.

Do not inventory every supplied metric or news item. Use a number only when it helps the reader understand magnitude. Use recent developments when they materially sharpen the interpretation of the measured findings. Treat news reports as reported developments, not as proof of a broader causal claim.

Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.

diagnostics.text: Current AI use is reported by 24.6% of businesses, while 28.6% expect to use it within six months. The four-percentage-point gap shows that stated near-term plans still exceed deployment. Among adults ages 18–64, 60.8% report some generative-AI use, although that consumer measure covers a different population and technology category. EE Times reported that Palo Alto Networks expanded into enterprise AI through a $4.5 billion deal. The transaction shows a supplier adding enterprise exposure; it does not establish that business adoption has accelerated.
